title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: in-product diagnostics for case access, security filters and holds
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned diagnostics, rollout windows and existing governance controls. Minor corrections should preserve Microsoft's tentative rollout wording and clarify the existing case-access and Help-pane guidance.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans self-service diagnostics that highlight misconfigurations involving case permissions, security filters and policy status.
claims.quote: Self-service diagnostics help identify common issues with case permissions, security filters, and policy status. The experience highlights potential misconfigurations and provides simple guidance

claims.claim: There are three planned checks covering case access, security filters and hold-policy distribution.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery is introducing three read-only diagnostic checks for case access, security filters, and hold-policy distribution.

claims.claim: The new checks are read-only.
claims.quote: Admins can use three read-only diagnostics to understand common issues with case access, search scoping, and hold-policy distribution.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the three new in-product diagnostics.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview eDiscovery in-product diagnostics case access security filters hold distribution 565222; "eDiscovery" "diagnostics" "case access". Opened edisc-permissions, edisc-settings-access-permissions and purview-compliance-diagnostics; only existing diagnostics described.

claims.claim: The portal location of the three new checks has not been documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview eDiscovery diagnostics case access security filter hold distribution enable disable default roles prerequisites licensing price. Opened edisc-permissions, edisc-settings-access-permissions and purview-compliance-diagnostics; no location for the new checks found.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified exactly what data each new check inspects or displays.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview eDiscovery in-product diagnostics case access security filters hold distribution 565222. Read MC1515937; opened edisc-settings-access-permissions and purview-compliance-diagnostics. No inspection or result fields for these three checks found.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The role needed to run the new diagnostics, including access for ordinary case members, has not been specified.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview eDiscovery diagnostics case access security filter hold distribution enable disable default roles prerequisites licensing price. Read MC1515937; opened edisc-permissions and purview-compliance-diagnostics. Existing RBAC diagnostic roles do not identify roles for the new checks.

claims.quote: Searched: Purview eDiscovery diagnostics case access security filter hold distribution enable disable default roles prerequisites licensing price. Read MC1515937; opened edisc-get-started, edisc-permissions and purview-compliance-diagnostics. No diagnostics-specific switch found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed how the new checks read the existing case, role, filter or hold controls.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview eDiscovery in-product diagnostics case access security filters hold distribution 565222. Read MC1515937; opened edisc-permissions, edisc-settings-access-permissions, edisc-search-permission-filtering and edisc-hold-manage. No mapping to the new checks found.

claims.claim: The notice points readers to existing topics for case permissions, security filters and hold distribution.
claims.quote: Learn about access and permission settings in eDiscovery cases (role/permission troubleshooting)- Security-filter diagnostic- Hold-distribution diagnostic

claims.claim: The cited access and permissions article does not mention a diagnostic.
claims.quote: Searched: diagnostic in the full opened edisc-settings-access-permissions article. It documents case users, role groups and guest access, not diagnostics.

claims.claim: The case-access article requires users to be added to the eDiscovery Manager role group.
claims.quote: before a user can access an eDiscovery case (and perform tasks in the case), you must add the user to the eDiscovery Manager role group

claims.claim: Case access depends on case membership.
claims.quote: For users who aren't eDiscovery Administrators, the cases shown are limited to those where the user is a member.
claims.fix: Qualify the sentence as: 'For users who are not eDiscovery Administrators, case visibility is limited to cases they belong to; search permissions filters govern what a manager may search.' The cited permissions page also says an eDiscovery Administrator can view and access all cases.

claims.claim: Search permissions filters restrict which mailboxes, sites and content an eDiscovery manager can search.
claims.quote: Use search permissions filtering to let an eDiscovery manager search only a subset of mailboxes and sites in your organization.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Adding or removing a role from a case-member role group automatically removes that group from every case it belongs to.
claims.quote: If you add or remove a role from a role group that you added as a member of a case, the role group is automatically removed as a member of the case (or any case the role group is a member of).

claims.claim: Assigning eDiscovery permissions requires Organization Management membership or the Role Management role.
claims.quote: You need to be a member of the Organization Management role group or be assigned the Role Management role to assign eDiscovery permissions in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: The eDiscovery Manager role group is edited at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Role groups > eDiscovery Manager > Edit.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Role groups. ... On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select eDiscovery Manager. ... Select Edit.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group> adds a security group to the role group.
claims.quote: You can add a mail-enabled security group ... by using the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group>

claims.claim: Case users are added at Microsoft Purview portal > eDiscovery > Cases > case > Case settings > Access and permissions > Users > Add.
claims.quote: Select the eDiscovery solution card and then select Cases ... Select a case, then select Case settings. ... select Access and permissions. ... Under Users, select Add

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseId}/caseMembers adds a user or role-group case member.
claims.quote: The ediscoveryCaseMember can be one of two types: a user or a role group. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/b0073e4e-4184-41c6-9eb7-8c8cc3e2288b/caseMembers

claims.claim: No portal UI for configuring search permissions filters was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview eDiscovery search permissions filtering configure portal UI New-ComplianceSecurityFilter. Opened edisc-search-permission-filtering and searched its portal/UI text. Configuration is documented through four Security & Compliance PowerShell cmdlets; no UI path found.

claims.claim: New-ComplianceSecurityFilter -FilterName <name of filter> -Users <user or role group> -Filters <filter> creates a search permissions filter.
claims.quote: New-ComplianceSecurityFilter -FilterName <name of filter> -Users <user or role group> -Filters <filter>

claims.claim: Compliance security filter cmdlets require Organization Management membership and the eDiscovery administrator role.
claims.quote: To run the compliance security filter cmdlets, you need to be a member of the Organization Management role group and have the eDiscovery administrator role assigned in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Search permissions filter cmdlets use Security & Compliance PowerShell with a connection to Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: You need to connect to both Exchange Online and Security & Compliance PowerShell to use the compliance security filter cmdlets.

claims.claim: Get-ComplianceSecurityFilter lists existing search permissions filters.
claims.quote: Use Get-ComplianceSecurityFilter to return a list of search permissions filters.

claims.claim: A hold policy can be retried at Microsoft Purview portal > eDiscovery > Cases > case > Hold policies > hold policy > Policy actions > Retry policy.
claims.quote: Select the eDiscovery solution card, then select Cases ... Select a case, then select the Hold policies tab. ... select the hold policy ... select Policy actions > Retry policy.

claims.claim: Get-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity <policyname> -DistributionDetail retrieves hold distribution details.
claims.quote: $status = Get-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity <policyname> -DistributionDetail ... Get-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity "policyname" -DistributionDetail | Select -ExpandProperty DistributionResults

claims.claim: Set-CaseHoldPolicy with RetryDistribution redeploys a hold policy.
claims.quote: Run the Set-CaseHoldPolicy -Identity "policyname" -RetryDistribution to resolve the issue. ... Set-CaseHoldPolicy "policyname" -RetryDistribution

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The existing eDiscovery RBAC diagnostic is found through Help > Diag:edisRBACdiag in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Select the Help control in the top right of the Microsoft Purview portal. Enter Diag:edisRBACdiag in search ... to run the eDiscovery RBAC Check test.
claims.fix: The cited permissions page supports this shortcut, but https://learn.microsoft.com/troubleshoot/microsoft-365/purview/diagnostics/purview-compliance-diagnostics gives an additional step. Replace the parenthesis with '(Help > Ask a question > search for Diag:edisRBACdiag; the permissions article abbreviates this to Help search)' and cite that diagnostics page.

claims.claim: The existing RBAC diagnostic checks Search, Export and Preview role assignments for a designated user.
claims.quote: Run the following diagnostic test to check if the Export, Preview, or Search roles are assigned to the designated admin account. ... enter the UPN or email address of the user

claims.claim: The permissions article says a user whose data is analysed with premium eDiscovery features needs Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5.
claims.quote: To analyze a user's data when premium eDiscovery features are enabled, the user must be assigned an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license.

claims.claim: The permissions article alternatively names Microsoft Purview Suite or Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-ons for E1 or E3 users.
claims.quote: users with an Office 365 E1 or an Office 365 or Microsoft 365 E3 license can be assigned a Microsoft Purview Suite ... or Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.

claims.claim: The permissions article does not identify a licence rule for the new diagnostics.
claims.quote: Searched: license and diagnostic in the opened edisc-permissions article. Read its licensing paragraph and RBAC diagnostic instructions; the three new diagnostic checks are not described or assigned an entitlement there.

claims.claim: The new checks do not automatically remediate configuration; any configuration fix is separate from their guidance.
claims.quote: The diagnostics provide guidance without changing your organization's existing configuration.
